title: fix(console): signing out no longer hands your list's filter, search and sort to the next person who signs in
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbYDsRkn71tNER7aYHM8b1BP)_

Fixes #29174

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：会话结束时（点「退出登录」或会话过期），Console 跳到登录页所带的回跳链接 `?redirect=` 只保留列表的路径和其它参数（如 `recordId`），去掉列表的 `uf_*` 状态（筛选、搜索、排序、分组、快速筛选、标签页）。下一个在同一浏览器登录的人回到同一个列表，看到的是自己保存的状态或视图默认值，首个数据请求不再带上一个人的条件。
- **为什么改**：共享电脑上 A 退出、B 登录，B 会打开 A 的筛选、搜索和排序，而筛选值可能是敏感信息（客户名、金额、搜索词）。这是 18.3.0 RC 中 P1 条目 `records-forms.adhoc-filter-sort-builder` 的 A3、N2 失败项。
- **风险与回滚**：低。只改回跳链接的拼装，两个登录页都没动；没有列表状态时回跳链接逐字节不变；邀请链接不受影响。代价：同一用户会话过期后重新登录，回到同一列表，筛选面板、排序、搜索从本人存储恢复，但快速筛选标签和工具栏分组回到视图默认；未登录者打开带列表状态的分享链接，登录后落在该列表，用自己的状态而不是链接里的。回滚即回退本 PR。
- **先看**：`ui/apps/console/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx`（`LoginRedirect`）；`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/userFilterUrlState.ts`（`withoutListStateParams`）；新测试 `ui/apps/console/src/components/ProtectedRoute.signOutListState-29174.test.tsx`。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run apps/console/src/components/ProtectedRoute.signOutListState-29174.test.tsx`，预期 4 个用例全部通过；第一个用例断言 A 退出后登录页地址不含 `uf_` 和 "pipeline"，B 登录后落在 `/apps/demo/demo_task/view/in_progress?recordId=r1`。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**The sign-in page's return link leaves the list's state behind.** When a session ends, the Console's signed-out guard (`LoginRedirect` in `ui/apps/console/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx`) sends the visitor to `/login?redirect=…`, and the Console login page follows that link after any successful sign-in. The guard built the link from the whole path and query, so a list's `uf_*` state rode into whoever signed in next. It now composes the link from the path plus every param that is not in the `uf_` family. When the URL carried no list state, the link keeps the original query byte for byte, so existing deep links do not change.

**One helper, in the module that owns the `uf_` family.** `withoutListStateParams(searchParams)` in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/userFilterUrlState.ts` returns a copy without any `uf_*` param (the four toolbar keys, quick-filter `uf_<field>` and `uf__tab`), keeping every other param in order. It reuses the module's own prefix, so no second copy of the naming exists. It is exported from `@object-ui/app-shell`, which is `"private": true`, so no published surface widens (`Clause-②: no` as claimed).

**Where the list then opens.** With no `uf_*` state in the URL, the list seeds from the signing-in user's own stored state (`objectViewListUrlState.ts`, seed leg 2: their Filter panel conditions and sort from their preferences, their search term from their per-user cache), or the view's default. B's storage is keyed by B's id, so nothing of A's is read.

No server change, no metadata key or option, and neither login page is edited (so nothing overlaps #29136 or #29105). Rows were always read under the signing-in user's permissions; this is a state carry-over fix, not an access fix.

## Tests

- `ui/apps/console/src/components/ProtectedRoute.signOutListState-29174.test.tsx` (new), 4 cases, through the real `AuthProvider` over a scripted auth client, the real `ProtectedRoute` (`AuthGuard` + `LoginRedirect`) and the real Console `LoginPage`:
  1. the card's path: A is on a list URL carrying `uf__filter`, `uf__search`, `uf__sort`, `uf__group`, `uf_priority`, `uf__tab` and `recordId`; A signs out; the login page's URL carries no `uf_` param and none of A's values; B signs in on the form and lands on the list path with `recordId=r1` kept;
  2. an invitation redirect (`/login?redirect=/accept-invitation/inv_1`) still lands on the invitation;
  3. a signed-out arrival on a deep link with no list state keeps it byte for byte (`note=a%20b` stays `%20`);
  4. a signed-out arrival on a link carrying list state loses it too (the guard cannot tell who signs in).
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.listUrlState-11860.test.tsx`: one new describe, 3 cases, at the data source of the real `ObjectView` and `ListView`: A's URL as A left it puts A's filter, search and sort into the first data request (control); the handed-over URL puts none of it there and the view's declared sort applies; the next user's own stored state applies there with nothing of A's merged in.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/userFilterUrlState.withoutListState-29174.test.ts` (new), 6 cases: the whole `uf_` family goes, every other param stays in order, an empty-valued `uf_` param goes, the input is untouched, and params without list state come back equal.

## Acceptance notes

- **Which site, measured on `origin/main` `692e0dc8`.** The card offered the sign-out side or the login side. The only composer of a list URL into `/login` is the Console's `LoginRedirect`; app-shell's `AuthenticatedRoute` sends a bare `/login`, and app-shell's `DefaultLoginPage` never follows `?redirect=` (it navigates to `/`). The follower is the Console `LoginPage` (`window.location.assign`). The guard was chosen because it is the single producer and needs no record of who left. A login-side drop would have needed that record to tell users apart, would still show A's values (the search term "pipeline") in the login page's address bar and history, and would have three followers to patch (login, register, verify-email-prompt), which all forward `?redirect=`.
- **Same-user session expiry.** At the guard, an explicit sign-out and an expired or revoked session look the same (the auth context only says the user is gone), and telling them apart would need new state in `@object-ui/auth`. So both drop the list state, and the user's own return path (the list's path and other params) is kept. Measured in the real browser below: a user who typed a search, signed out and signed back in got their own search back from their per-user storage. Quick-filter chips and a toolbar grouping are not in per-user storage, so they fall back to the view's.
- **A signed-out visitor opening a shared list link** now lands on that list after signing in, on their own state rather than the link's (test case 4). A visitor already signed in still opens the link's state exactly as before.
- **Kept as non-list-state params:** `recordId`, `tab`, a related list's `filter[FIELD]` scoping, and any other param outside the `uf_` family. A `/login?redirect=…` URL composed elsewhere (bookmarked or typed) is still followed as written; the login pages are unchanged.
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx` gains one bullet under "A user's list state never writes the view".

## Verification

All readings below are at head `a1fa3999` (this branch merged with `origin/main` `74a19dd8`) unless a line names another head.

<details>
<summary>Tests: 19 files, 194 passed</summary>

`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run` on the three test files above plus the 16 nearest suites (the Console's `App` route tests, `RootLandingRedirect`, `SetupRoute`, `StudioRoute` ×3, `FormPage.predicateScope`, `AcceptInvitationRoute`, `i18nAfterSignIn-12034`, `internalFormShell`, `ObjectView.ufViewSwitch-11992`, `userFilterUrlState.listState-11860` and the app-shell product-neutral ratchet): 19 files, 194 passed, 0 failed. The same set read 194/194 at `97150043` (before either merge) and at `13da5477` (after the first).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Ablations: both go red, both restored to HEAD</summary>

Run with `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which restores the file and checks its blob against HEAD.

1. Restore the verbatim redirect in `LoginRedirect` (`const redirect = location.pathname + returnSearch;` becomes `location.pathname + location.search`): the Console test file reads 2 failed, 2 passed. Red: "A signs out of a filtered, searched, sorted list; B signs in and lands on the path with none of it" and "a signed-out arrival on a link carrying list state loses the list state". Green, as they should be: the invitation redirect and the deep link with no list state. Restored blob `30df279f` == HEAD.
2. Make the helper keep every param (`if (!key.startsWith(PREFIX)) kept.append(…)` becomes an unconditional append): 7 failed, 34 passed across the three test files (the two Console cases above, three helper cases, and the two ObjectView cases that read the handed-over URL). Restored blob `44703363` == HEAD.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Real browser: the card's path on a stock showcase boot</summary>

Playwright (Chromium) against a fresh `showcase` boot built from this branch at `97150043`, through the real Console sign-in form. A is the seeded admin. B is a second member, invited, signed up and accepted on the same server. Both used the same browser context, as on a shared computer.

- A opened `/apps/com.example.showcase/showcase_task/view/in_progress` with `uf__filter` (estimate_hours > 10 and progress < 80), `uf__search=pipeline` and `uf__sort` (due_date desc). A's first data request carried `search=pipeline`, `sort=-due_date` and both conditions.
- A signed out from the Account menu. The login page's URL was `/_console/login?redirect=%2Fapps%2Fcom.example.showcase%2Fshowcase_task%2Fview%2Fin_progress`, with no `uf_` and no "pipeline".
- B signed in on that page and landed on `/_console/apps/com.example.showcase/showcase_task/view/in_progress` with no `uf_`. B's first data request carried only the view's own filter (`status = in_progress`), with no search, no sort and none of A's conditions.
- Control: B signing in on a `/login?redirect=` that holds A's state verbatim (what the guard composed before this change) lands with `uf_` in the URL, and B's first data request carries A's search, sort and both conditions.
- Same user: A typed a search in the toolbar, signed out and signed back in. A's own search came back from A's per-user storage (the URL re-mirrored `uf__search=pipeline` and the first request carried `search=pipeline`). In the same browser, B signing in after A got the view's default.

</details>
